what: The 'C50/'C51 discriminator: write through the DSP's data space, read back through program space, and sample PMST
board: 25 MHz Courier V.Everything 2806, serial 22AEB36ACKND, ID_SDL v4.03d, supervisor 7.4.16, DSP 3.1.2

result.0x0800: data write lands (a55a, 5aa5 read back); program space returns ffff both times - not the same memory
result.0x1800: same - program space unaffected by the write
result.0x2400: program space follows the write exactly (a55a then 5aa5) - writable memory

conclusion: MP/MC=0 and PMST.RAM=1, so on a 'C50 the 9K SARAM would be mapped into program space over 0x0800-0x2BFF and both 0x0800 and 0x1800 would follow the write. They do not, and 0x2400 does. That is the 'C51 map: 8K on-chip ROM at 0x0000-0x1FFF winning over SARAM in program space, with writable memory above it.
offline_control: the emulator fixture, which maps a 4K ROM at 0x0000-0x0fff and SARAM above, produces the opposite split at 0x0800 vs 0x1800/0x2400 - so the instrument shows both signatures
